newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Aug 26.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Aug 26.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Aluminium producer Comalco Ltd said on Monday the longer term outlook for the company was strong despite a sharply lower profit for the half year to June 30, 1996. Comalco's pre-abnormal net on a joint venture basis was A$43.9 million. Analysts had expected a pre-abnormals net of between A$55 million and A$67 million.

The wage deal struck between Qantas Airways Ltd and the Transport Workers Union (TWU) on Friday, under which TWU workers receive an eight percent pay rise over two years, was seen as positive for Qantas by aviation analysts.

The management-led buyout group that won the bidding for Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer film studio with a US$1.3 billion bid is looking for a US$800 million loan package to fund the acquisition and provide working capital. Sources close to the group, which includes billionaire Kirk Kerkorian's Tracinda Corp and Seven Network Ltd, said US$450 million of the amount would be used to help fund the deal with US$350 million going for operations.

Caltex Petroleum Corp said no decision has been made on selling down its stake in Caltex Australia Ltd, refusing to confirm market reports it plans to reduce the holding to 51 pct from the current 75 pct. Newspapers reported that had broker First Pacific tried to sell a A$218 million parcel of Caltex Corp's shares to institutions on Friday.

Australian retail giant Coles Myer Ltd has not revived plans to break up into constituent units, chairman Nobby Clark said on Sunday. "Let me say now that the board is not considering any proposals such as that at this time," Clark said in a television interview when asked if the idea of splitting the group up had resurfaced.

Reef Casino Trust, operator of the Cairns casino in northern Queensland, said late on Friday results for the year to June 30, 1997 would be lower than prospectus forecasts. Reef earlier reported a maiden net loss of A$26.80 million in 1995/96 for the period from its opening in January 31.
Shares reinstated after suspension on Friday. Company says it will defecnt Supreme Court proceedings brought against it by IOOF Australia Trustees Ltd.
